Sampled HR@10 can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation; preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator, but describe results specifically as sampled-candidate performance ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). For candidate–incumbent comparisons, retain paired per-user hit indicators. Within each category, resample 200 user pairs with replacement, recompute their mean hit difference, then average the four category differences equally. Repeat, e.g., 10,000 times for a bootstrap interval; keep each user’s candidates unchanged. Pairing requires identical resampled indices for both models ([SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). If identities overlap across categories, resample those identities jointly to preserve dependence.

These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted checkpoints, observed histories, fixed candidates and training seed 42. They exclude candidate-resampling, retraining, split and seed variability; bootstrap repetitions cannot replace independent training runs ([Bouthillier et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03098)). Repeated adaptive validation queries also introduce selection optimism: an ordinary bootstrap interval computed after choosing the winner does not correct it ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)).

Suggested prespecified search rule: before running ablations, fix their order, maximum comparisons, minimum practical macro improvement δ, category-regression tolerance and GPU-time allocation, including failures. Accept only when observed macro gain exceeds δ and category guardrails pass; optionally require a multiplicity-adjusted paired lower bound above zero, while acknowledging that adaptive selection still limits inference. Treat inconclusive gains as insufficient evidence to replace the incumbent. Record every attempted configuration, paired differences and elapsed GPU time; stop at 43,200 GPU-seconds. These are proposed operational safeguards, not a guarantee against validation overfitting; keep held-out evaluation untouched.
